subject: Architecture
title: Space Elevators: The Ultimate Tall Building
description: One-minute skill: Space Elevators: The Ultimate Tall Building.

hook.text: A space elevator would be a cable from Earth's surface to orbit — 22,000 miles tall.

buildup.text: Climber vehicles would ride the cable, carrying cargo to space at a fraction of rocket costs.

discovery.text: Carbon nanotubes could theoretically create a cable strong enough — but nobody can make them long enough yet.

twist.text: Japan's Obayashi Corporation has announced plans to build a space elevator by 2050. Engineers are skeptical.

climax.text: If built, a space elevator would reduce launch costs from $10,000 per pound to under $100.

punchline.text: The tallest structure ever built would make the Burj look like a speed bump.

quiz.question: What material could theoretically make a space elevator cable?

details.summary: A space elevator would be a cable stretching from Earth's surface to geostationary orbit at 36,000 kilometers, with climber vehicles carrying cargo and passengers to space. While theoretically possible, no material yet exists with sufficient strength-to-weight ratio to build the cable.
details.whyItMatters: The space elevator represents the ultimate extension of the 'tall building' concept. If realized, it would revolutionize space access, reducing launch costs by orders of magnitude and enabling space-based industry.
takeaways: A space elevator would extend 36,000 km to geostationary orbit
No material yet has the strength-to-weight ratio for the cable
It would revolutionize space access if materials challenges are solved

faq.question: What material could a space elevator cable be made from?
faq.answer: Carbon nanotubes or graphene ribbons have the theoretical strength, but manufacturing defect-free strands at the required lengths remains far beyond current capability. A single flaw in billions of meters of cable could cause catastrophic failure. Material science is the primary bottleneck.

faq.question: Has anyone seriously tried to build a space elevator?
faq.answer: Japan's Obayashi Corporation announced plans for a space elevator by 2050. NASA and JAXA have funded small-scale experiments. An annual Space Elevator Conference discusses progress. The concept is taken seriously by engineers but remains decades away from practical realization.
